reason: The hypothesis directly transfers the observation that a Hf-containing alloy (W29Ta42Cr5V16Hf8) showed no precipitates to a different alloy (W38Ta36Cr15V11) by proposing a specific Hf microalloying intervention (~8 at.% substituting Cr) to suppress Cr-V precipitates. This is a straightforward application of a result already implied by the comparison of the two alloys in the research question and passages P1/P5, without introducing a new mechanism or resolving a conflict; the mechanism (enhanced lattice distortion reducing solute mobility) is a well-known concept from the HEA radiation tolerance literature (P10, P11, P12, P29).

provenance.mechanism: P10, P11, P12, P29, general knowledge

copied_elements: W38Ta36Cr15V11 baseline composition and its Cr-V precipitate formation at ~8 dpa (P1, P5, P6)
W29Ta42Cr5V16Hf8 shows no precipitates at 10 dpa (research question context, implied from P1/P5)
Hf addition suppresses precipitates (implied from comparison of two alloys in research question)
Lattice distortion and reduced solute mobility as radiation tolerance mechanism (P10, P11, P12, P29)
